workflow: LangGraph linear: load -> intent -> keyword_plan -> title -> meta_description -> headings -> content -> media -> internal_links -> eeat -> aeo_geo -> structured_data -> social_meta -> technical -> fact_check -> qa -> site -> write

checklist.description: Decide the page's primary query, search intent, user-journey stage, real user questions and topic-cluster role. Every later skill builds on this.
Build the page keyword map (primary, secondary, semantic variants, placements) and measure current keyword stuffing. Deterministic; its limits are enforced on every generated text.
Write a unique, intent-matching <title> (30-60 chars) that leads with the primary query and ends with the brand.
Write a 120-160 character meta description that answers the query in one line and gives a reason to click.
Produce one H1 and a logical H2/H3 outline (question-shaped where users ask questions) that maps the page to the search intent.
Rewrite the page body answer-first (direct answer -> details -> extras) as typed semantic blocks (p, ul, ol, table, dl, figure, blockquote) using the client's own images.
Write descriptive alt text and captions for every page image, and flag technical image issues (size, format, lazy loading, dimensions).
Improve anchor text and add contextual internal links that connect the page to its topic cluster and the next step in the user journey.
Strengthen Experience, Expertise, Authoritativeness and Trust signals with packet-backed author info, credentials, dates, sources and trust elements.
Make the page easy for answer engines and generative AI to quote - summary/TL;DR, definition sentence, FAQ from real user questions, consistent entity statements.

Produce a JSON-LD @graph for the page (WebPage/ProfilePage, Person/Organization, WebSite, BreadcrumbList, FAQPage, ItemList, Article, HowTo when steps exist) that mirrors the expected visible content.
Derive Open Graph and Twitter/X card tags from the expected title, description and the best available image. Deterministic.
Page-level technical on-page checks from the exploration JSON - canonical, robots meta, lang, viewport, URL slug, hreflang, JS-only content, broken links, image weight. Deterministic.
Verify every number, date and named claim in the expected content against the exploration JSON, and flag stale years, versions and missing modified dates. Deterministic.
Final pass - site-wide uniqueness of titles/descriptions/H1s, checklist scoring before vs after, priorities, rendered HTML preview of the expected page. Deterministic.

how_to_review: Open pages/<id>.json: each change has current, expected and reference (file/line to edit). Approve, then apply manually. needs_verification = contains facts not found in the exploration JSON.
